chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and others, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
"If he has intercourse a second time before he expiates, then upon him is another expiation; there is no difference of opinion in this."

key_terms.اخْتِلَافٌ: Difference of opinion or dispute among scholars.
key_terms.الظِّهَار: Dhikr, a specific form of divorce in Islamic law where a husband compares his wife to his mother's back.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation, a ritual penalty or act of worship required to atone for a specific violation.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband has intercourse multiple times before expiating Dhikr?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that each instance of sexual intercourse before the completion of the *kaffarah* for *Zihar* incurs a separate expiation, a ruling (*hukm*) noted as undisputed (*laysa fihi ikhtilaf*) among jurists. It underscores the cumulative nature of the penalty, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the literal application of the Quranic verse regarding the freeing of a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor as sequential obligations.
